evals.name: blog-schema-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I'm starting a new Next.js app with Postgres (plain node-postgres driver) and want to use drizzle. Set up the schema for a simple blog: users, posts, and comments. Users can write many posts, posts have many comments, and comments belong to a user and a post. Also add tags with a many-to-many to posts. Use snake_case in the database but camelCase in my code. Include the drizzle config and relations so I can use db.query.
evals.expected_output: A schema.ts using pgTable with generatedAlwaysAsIdentity PKs, snake_case handling, exported models, array-form indexes where used; a relations.ts using defineRelations (v1 API) with .through() for the posts<->tags many-to-many; a drizzle.config.ts with dialect/schema/out/dbCredentials; a db.ts passing { relations } to drizzle().
assertions: All schema models (tables, enums) are exported
Relations use the v1 defineRelations API, not the legacy relations() helper
The posts-to-tags many-to-many uses .through() on the junction table columns
Snake_case is handled via the snakeCase builder or explicit column name aliases (camelCase TS keys do not silently become camelCase DB columns)
drizzle.config.ts includes dialect, schema path, and dbCredentials
The db initialization passes relations to drizzle() so db.query works
Primary keys use generatedAlwaysAsIdentity (or an explicitly justified alternative), not bare serial without comment

evals.name: review-buggy-rqb-code
evals.expected_output: A review that catches: (1) orderBy using imported table objects instead of the callback parameter in relational queries, with corrected code; (2) sql.raw() with interpolated user input is SQL injection — fix with parameterized sql`` or ilike operator; (3) extras referencing the imported table and using a raw aggregate subquery — should use the callback parameter and db.$count. Corrected code for each.
assertions: Identifies that orderBy in relational queries must use the callback parameter, not the imported table object, and explains why (aliasing in nested scopes)
Provides corrected orderBy code using the callback form
Flags sql.raw() with interpolated user input as SQL injection and provides a parameterized fix
Fixes the extras block to use the callback parameter (and db.$count or equivalent for the count)
Does not introduce new API mistakes (e.g., mixing v0 and v1 idioms)

evals.name: migration-workflow-advice
evals.prompt: Our team of 5 has been using `drizzle-kit push` against our shared staging Postgres since the prototype days and now we're about to launch. Two questions: how should we set up migrations properly for production + CI, and how do we handle a data backfill (we're splitting a `name` column into `first_name`/`last_name`) as part of that?
evals.expected_output: Advice to switch from push to generate+migrate for the team/production context, with the concrete commands, config, and the __drizzle_migrations tracking table explained; a warning about not mixing push and generate against the same database and how to baseline; use of drizzle-kit generate --custom for the backfill SQL so it lives in the ordered migration history; mention of drizzle-kit check for team race conditions.
assertions: Recommends generate + migrate (not push) for the team/production scenario and explains why push no longer fits
Warns about mixing push and generate histories against the same database and addresses how to transition/baseline
Recommends drizzle-kit generate --custom (custom migration) for the backfill SQL so it stays in the versioned history
Shows the actual commands and where migration files/tracking live (out folder, __drizzle_migrations)
Mentions team-safety tooling such as drizzle-kit check or committing snapshots/journal to version control
